source_text: Pervenire autem et ad innocentes gratiam Christi, ad quos Adae culpa non pervenit, propter quod vigilanter inculcavit: Multo magis gratia Dei et donum unius hominis Iesu Christi in plures abundavit [n203] , ut illa superior coaequatio eius aetatis, quae ratione utitur, in contrariis studiis indicet imitationem, haec autem in gratiae largitate praelatio consecratos et provectos approbet innocentes. Quae cum ita sint, tibi, non mihi Apostolum obviare senti, contra te eum arma ferre cognoscito, qui dogma tuum praeceptorisque tui Fausti, a quo es velut prima manu tinctus, hoc uno, si cetera deessent, vehementer everteret, quia dicit per unius inoboedientiam multos, non omnes peccatores constitutos fuisse et per unius oboedientiam iustos non omnes constitutos fuisse, sed multos. Ut enim diligenter, quam tibi sermo hic repugnet, lectoris intellegentiae suggeratur, Apostolus pronuntiat non omnes per Adam peccatores constitutos fuisse, tu dicis omnes omnino per Adam peccato naturali ad ius diaboli pertinere; ambigi non potest inter te et Apostolum magnam esse pugnam.
pass_a_gloss: But that the grace of Christ arrives even at innocents, to whom Adam's fault did not arrive, on account of which he vigilantly stamped in: Much more the grace of God and the gift of one human being Jesus Christ abounded unto more, so that that superior co-equation of that age which uses reason may indicate imitation in contrary pursuits, but this preference in the largess of grace may approve consecrated and advanced innocents. Which things being so, feel that the Apostle opposes you, not me; know that he bears arms against you, who would vehemently overturn your dogma and that of your teacher Faustus, by whom you were dyed as if by a first hand, by this one thing, if the rest were lacking, because he says that through the disobedience of one many, not all, were constituted sinners and through the obedience of one not all were constituted just, but many. For that it may be diligently supplied to the reader's understanding how this speech is repugnant to you, the Apostle pronounces that not all were constituted sinners through Adam, you say that all altogether through Adam by a natural sin belong to the devil's right; it cannot be doubted that there is a great fight between you and the Apostle.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS donum; Blaise grace-gift vs inherited sin
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Christ’s grace also reaches the innocent, whom Adam’s fault does not reach. That is why he carefully emphasized: ‘Much more did God’s grace and the gift of the one man Jesus Christ abound to more people’ (Romans 5:15). The earlier comparison of equals thus indicates imitation in opposite pursuits among people old enough to use reason; this preference for grace’s generosity, however, establishes that the innocent are consecrated and advanced. Since this is so, recognize that the apostle opposes you, not me; understand that he bears arms against you. Even if everything else were lacking, this one point would powerfully overthrow your doctrine and that of your teacher Faustus, by whom you received your first coloring, so to speak: he says that through one man’s disobedience many, not all, were made sinners, and through one man’s obedience not all but many were made righteous (Romans 5:19). To make the reader understand carefully how this statement opposes you: the apostle declares that not all were made sinners through Adam. You say that absolutely all belong to the devil’s jurisdiction through Adam by natural sin. There can be no doubt of the great conflict between you and the apostle.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Rom 5 contrast of Adam's offense and Christ's gift; keep gift, not later 'grace system'.
